why: The two trackers render the same shape of fact and had drifted into two
designs and two vocabularies. Neither side could say which one was current,
because each had changed its own copy since the other last looked. This file
is the single answer. It is data, not code: the products share no database,
no REST namespace and no build, and coupling them through shared code would
be worse than the drift. What they share is this contract, and each side has
a test that fails when its own markup stops matching it.

structure.note: Every class below is written as a SUFFIX. A product renders it with its own prefix and a hyphen: suffix 'card-rail' is 'alt-card-rail' in the layoff tracker and 'tit-card-rail' in the talent tracker. A product may carry extra classes on the same element (its existing colour and state classes), but the contract class must be present.

rail.card-employer: The employer, set in the serif face. Never a link colour unless it is a link.
rail.card-industry: Optional. Omitted entirely when the record carries none; never rendered empty.
rail.card-where: Location, or the not-stated string wrapped in card-nowhere. Never blank.

body.card-h: The fact, in one line. Link colour only when it links somewhere.
body.card-rt: The plain-English read of the record, visually separated from the sourced fact above it. Optional only because a record may carry nothing to say.

foot.card-when: The date the SOURCE carries, or the not-stated string. Rendered in a <time datetime> when there is a date.
foot.card-src: The publisher, as an outbound link with target=_blank and rel containing noopener. An archived copy may follow as a SECOND link, never instead.

badges.order_note: These three come first, in this order, always. Product-specific badges (the layoff tracker's AI attribution and reason tags) follow them.

card-ev.carries: the product's own evidence vocabulary, listed under evidence_labels

card-amt.required: only when the record carries an amount
card-amt.omitted_when: there is no amount. The direction badge already says 'Headcount Not Stated'; a second badge saying the same thing was the duplicate this contract removed.
card-amt.carries: a number plus a real text unit, never a CSS ::after

direction_labels_note: The stored keys are the two products' own and are NOT shared: the layoff
tracker has no signal_direction column and derives its key from whether the
record carries a headcount. What is shared is the four strings.
'Adding Roles' replaced 'Hiring up' in the talent tracker because 'up' was
doing the work of 'the source told us headcount is going up', which a reader
has to reverse-engineer. 'Cutting Roles' is its opposite in the same shape.
'Headcount Not Stated' is the bucket for a record whose source says nothing
about headcount at all. It is not an other-category, and naming it that way
is truer to the rule that neither product infers a direction its source did
not state. Title Case, not sentence case: the owner has asked for Title Case
three times, tests/php/render_dashboard.php enforces it on the talent
tracker's display labels, and these four strings are quoted in Title Case in
the decision that created this contract. The general sentence-case house
rule still governs every label OUTSIDE this vocabulary.

alt.note: Every row this product holds is a cut, so 'Adding Roles' and 'Pay Change' never appear here. They are absent, never renamed and never reused for something else.

evidence_labels.note: Each product's evidence vocabulary is its own, because the evidence really is different. What the contract fixes is the SLOT: second badge, always present, always carrying words rather than colour alone.

not_stated.note: Said out loud, never left blank and never guessed. Both strings are shared verbatim.

copy_rules.colour_never_alone: Every badge carries its own words. A reader who cannot see the colour loses nothing.

no_aria_label_over_visible_text: An aria-label on an element that already has visible text REPLACES that
text for a screen reader. The talent tracker shipped longer, invisible,
differently-worded labels over its visible ones and they read as a
different page. Inside a card, aria-label is allowed only on an element
with no text of its own.
expander_is_a_button: Anything that opens more detail is a real <button type=button> carrying
aria-expanded, never a click handler on the row or the card. The layoff
tracker's expander was a mouse-only <tr> click and is now a button; it
a11y.title_is_never_the_only_copy: A title= attribute is a supplement. Nothing that a reader needs may live only there.

mobile.rule: The rail stacks above the body and nothing else changes; the reading order was already the order a reader needs. Nothing inside a card may set a fixed width or a min-width that exceeds the viewport. Long values wrap with overflow-wrap: anywhere rather than being clipped.
mobile.do_not_validate_with: scrollWidth === innerWidth. It passes on a clipped page, and both sites have an overflow-x rule on a narrow ancestor that makes the comparison meaningless.

changing_this_file: 1. Edit it in one repo, run that repo's card-contract test, and update the
2. Copy the file byte-for-byte into the sibling and do the same there.
3. Update the spec section in BOTH docs/TECHLOG.md.
Step 2 is not a convention anyone has to remember: card-contract.yml in each
repo fetches the sibling's copy and goes red while the two differ.
